advantages: Returns `true` only when every element matches the expected value; otherwise returns `false`.
Fails fast: stops checking as soon as a non-matching element is found.
Guards against invalid input by returning `false` when the input is not a filled array.

parameterDescriptions.expected: The element to compare each array item against.

shortDescription: `areEqual` checks whether all elements in an array are equal to a given expected value, returning `true` only for non-empty arrays where every item matches.
typeScriptHint: Use `areEqual` when you need a strict all-items check; it returns `false` for empty arrays and for any non-array or non-filled input.
useCase: Validate that a list contains only a single allowed value (e.g., all status flags are `true`, all roles are `"admin"`, or all numeric entries equal a required constant) while treating empty input as invalid (`false`).
